tone_statements.citation: Smolders, Joshua A. G. 2019. Nominal and verbal number in Bilugu Opo. Studies in African Linguistics 48(1): 133-184. doi:10.32473/sal.v48i1.114929
tone_statements.quote: Tone in Opo has a high lexical and grammatical functional load. According to my analysis there are four levels of phonemic tone in Bilugu: low (L), mid (M), high (H), and extra‑high (X). Extra-high is attested only on a subset of the vowels: /i u a/. The number of phonemic tone levels in the other dialects has not been fully analyzed, but based on current data there are possibly only three. Table 5 below gives evidence of four levels of contrast on monosyllabic, monomorphemic nouns in a M_H environment, using the frame /tā __ tɔ́n/ 'It is a big __'.
tone_statements.locator: sec. 1.5 Phonological overview, pp. 139-140 (Table 5 'Lexical tone contrast in Opo (Bilugu only)')

tone_statements.citation: Mellese Gelaneh Alemu. 2017 [title page dated 2016]. Documentation and Grammatical Description of Tapo. PhD dissertation, Addis Ababa University. xiv+236 pp.
tone_statements.quote: Tapo is a tonal language with three contrasting tones. Lemi (2010) and Abebe (2008) labeled the language as a High and Low contrastive tonal language. Van Silfhout (2013) adding the mid tone has identified three contrastive tone levels in Tapo. This study also agrees with the latter and analyzed the language as having three tone levels i.e. High (H), Mid (M) and Low (L) as the following minimal pairs given in 3.54 - 3.63 show. The tone bearing units in Tapo are vowels.
tone_statements.locator: sec. 3.4 Tone, p. 44 (minimal sets 3.54-3.63 on pp. 44-45)

tone.says: First-hand analysis: lexical and grammatical tone with high functional load; four phonemic levels L/M/H/X in Bilugu (X restricted to /i u a/), evidence from a four-way minimal set in the frame /tā __ tɔ́n/; other dialects possibly only three levels; verbal number partly marked by tonal alternation of verb stems (sec. 3).

tone.locator: sec. 3.4 Tone, p. 44 (minimal sets 3.54-3.63 on pp. 44-45)
tone.says: Tapo is tonal with three contrastive level tones H/M/L, TBU = vowel, minimal pairs/triplets given; reviews earlier two-level analyses (Lemi 2010, Abebe 2008) and van Silfhout's three levels; grammatical tone on verb-final vowels elsewhere in ch. 3. Note the competing four-level analysis of Smolders 2019 for Bilugu.
